title: Kernel defects found by dogfooding the harness on itself
description: Eight defects found by pointing general-verify at its own kernel. Each one lets the harness report a verdict it has not earned - either by letting the environment change the answer, by classifying a genuine red state as unobservable, or by a check quietly failing to catch what it claims to catch. All eight are fixed test-first, and every case here was observed failing before it passed.

clauses.text: The gate's verdict must not depend on the environment of whatever process invoked it.
clauses.observable_by: a test that runs the gate from inside another test runner still sees the inner suite's real FAIL
clauses.rationale: The gate inherited the parent environment wholesale, so NODE_TEST_CONTEXT leaked into the spawned runner and made a failing suite report success. A harness whose entire value is the verdict cannot let the caller's environment change it.

clauses.text: A test that fails because the code under test does not exist yet must be reported as FAIL, not BLOCKED.
clauses.observable_by: a test importing a missing module yields verdict FAIL
clauses.rationale: This is the classic TDD starting state and the primary workflow: write the test, watch it fail because nothing implements it yet, record the red proof. Classifying it BLOCKED made `general-verify red` refuse to record anything, breaking the mechanism the whole harness is built around.

clauses.text: The gate must report pass and fail counts whenever the runner prints them.
clauses.observable_by: a run of node --test yields counts.passed and counts.failed

clauses.text: Each runner's output parser must be testable directly, without spawning that toolchain.
clauses.observable_by: extractForRunner is exported and returns the failing names for captured pytest, go and cargo output
clauses.rationale: Output formats are the part of this kernel most likely to rot silently as runners change. A parser that can only be exercised by installing five toolchains will not be tested, and will therefore break unnoticed.

clauses.text: A Python test file must be recognised wherever the language permits one, not only under a tests directory.
clauses.observable_by: isTestFile returns true for test_slugify.py at a project root
clauses.rationale: A missed test file is scanned as source: its skipped tests are never reported, and its ordinary print statements are reported as shipped debug leftovers. The check fails in both directions at once.

clauses.text: The assertion-free check must not be satisfied by words appearing in a test's own name or in string literals.
clauses.observable_by: a test named with the word 'asserts' whose body contains no assertion is still reported
clauses.rationale: The searched body began at the declaration, so it included the test's own name. Any test named 'asserts ...', 'should ...' or 'throws ...' was silently exempted - which is a very large share of real test names, and precisely the ones a reviewer would assume were covered.

clauses.text: A focused or skipped test declaration must still be analysed for assertions.
clauses.observable_by: a focused test with no assertion is reported by both the focused check and the assertion-free check
clauses.rationale: The declaration pattern did not recognise a modifier like .only, so the worst combination available - a focused test that also asserts nothing - fell through the gap between the two checks.

clauses.text: A test-support module must not be analysed as though it were a test file.
clauses.observable_by: a helpers module in the test directory that builds test source as strings produces no assertion-free findings
clauses.rationale: Found while fixing A6. Helper, fixture and factory modules live in test directories and routinely contain test source as string literals - exactly the shape that fools a text-based analysis. A false positive here is worse than a miss: the first thing anyone does with a check that cries wolf is switch it off, after which it catches nothing at all.

non_goals: Contract, red-proof and stack-detection coverage. Those suites were written at the same time and passed immediately, so they are characterisation tests, not test-first work. They run in the gate and are deliberately NOT claimed as cases here - crediting them with red proofs they never earned would be exactly the dishonesty the red proof exists to prevent.
Adding new verifier categories. This contract is about the checks already claimed working actually working.
